records.name: Notsolatin
records.summary: A performance space and recording studio in Philadelphia that presents artists in an intimate setting. It has shows on Tuesdays and Fridays and Big-Band Sundays, and it was founded in 2018.
records.what_you_do: Go to a show and pay a suggested donation at the door, or join the mailing list through the site's sign up form. Artists can send booking inquiries.

schedule.text: Shows on Tuesdays and Fridays, with doors at 7 pm and the show at 7:30 pm. Big-Band Sundays are announced separately.

cost.text: Suggested $20 donation at the door. No tickets are sold in advance unless the group says otherwise.

first_step.how: Come to a Tuesday or Friday show (doors at 7 pm), pay the suggested $20 at the door, or join the mailing list through the site's sign up form.
first_step.basis: Shows are open to the public with a suggested donation, and the site gives a clear way to join the mailing list.
first_step.what_to_expect: Shows are held in a regular home at 1440 W. Ritner Street, which the group says is not a commercial venue. Doors open at 7 pm and the show starts at 7:30 pm, with seating first come, first served. You pay a suggested $20 at the door; the site does not say anything about step-free entry, restrooms, or age limits.
first_visit_tips: Doors open at 7 pm and the show starts at 7:30 pm.
Plan on the suggested $20 donation at the door, since tickets are not sold in advance.
Seating is first come, first served, so arrive a little early.
The group asks guests to be respectful, since the shows are in a home.

records.notes: The event list says there are no events at the moment and shows no readable dates. The contact page uses template placeholders (a 123 phone number, a generic email and a San Francisco footer address), so none of that is recorded. The accessibility statement link did not lead to readable content.

records.name: Oak Lane Presbyterian Church
records.summary: A community church in Oak Lane with Sunday worship, youth Sunday school, and community events such as a Soup and Sandwich event and a Winter Warmth Drive.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship at 11 am (10 am in summer), join youth Sunday school on Zoom, or help with the October soup and sandwich event or the winter drive.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am, and at 10 am in summer (summer services are held downstairs). Youth Sunday school at 9:30 am on Zoom.

locations.label: Church building (southeast corner of 11th Street and Oak Lane)

access.notes: The church's welcome page says the building has a wheelchair ramp, a chair lift, accessible restrooms, and extra-wide doors.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 11 am (10 am in summer), or call the office at 215-424-4446 first to ask about a first visit.
first_step.basis: The welcome page invites people without a church home nearby to make this congregation their own, and the site gives the fixed worship time and office contacts for a first visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 11 am, or at 10 am from late June, when the service moves downstairs to the air-conditioned room. The site does not say how long the service runs, what happens afterward, or whether anything costs money. Youth Sunday school meets at 9:30 am on Zoom.
first_visit_tips: In summer, worship starts at 10 am and is held downstairs, which the church describes as air-conditioned.
The building has a ramp, a chair lift, and extra-wide doors.
Call the office at 215-424-4446 to confirm the time before you come.

records.notes: Summer worship at 10 am starts June 28, 2026 and is held downstairs. No page read says how long the service runs or whether coffee follows, and children are not mentioned in the worship posts. The soup and winter drive posts give dates only (Oct 22 and Oct 17 and 24, 2026); the details are in flyer images that could not be read. A parking notice from February 2026 was mentioned in a site summary but not confirmed, so it is not recorded.

records.name: Old First United Church of Christ
records.summary: A United Church of Christ congregation near 4th and Race streets that worships on Sunday in person and on Zoom, hosts Sunday suppers, and runs historical tours.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship at 10 am or stay for fellowship at 11:15 am, come to a Sunday supper, help with the Saturday breakfast or the coat drive, join the newcomer brunch after service, or take a historical tour.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10 am, in person and on Zoom. Fellowship hour at 11:15 am. Sunday Suppers every week at 5 pm. Saturday breakfast every Saturday morning. Historical tours on Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays, 10 am to 1 pm.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10 am, in person or on Zoom. To join the newcomer brunch after service, tell the church in advance through the contact form.
first_step.basis: The site has a newcomer page, a newcomer brunch after worship, and a welcoming committee that can meet you before your first Sunday, and it says anyone is welcome as they are.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 10 am, in person or on Zoom, and the site says you do not have to agree to any set of beliefs to belong. The site does not say how long the service lasts or what to wear. After service, a newcomer group goes out for brunch or a drink in Center City or Old City, and the site does not list a cost for it.
first_visit_tips: If you want the newcomer brunch after service, tell the church first through the contact form.
Worship is also on Zoom if you would rather join from home.
The contact page has a parking pass link, so check it before you drive.
You can ask for coffee with the pastor before your first Sunday by calling 215-922-4566 or emailing admin@oldfirstucc.org.

records.notes: The breakfast post names October 31 but no year appears in its text, and the Sunday Suppers post is undated, so neither is used as last_sign_of_life. No page read gives worship length, dress, or accessibility details. The newcomer page's 'What to Expect' link was not followed. The breakfast is cooked by the church on the fifth Saturdays of the year; the church's partners cover other Saturdays.

records.name: Old Pine Street Presbyterian Church
records.summary: A historic Presbyterian church on Pine Street with a 10:30 am Sunday service, Sunday school for young children during worship, and a concert program.
records.what_you_do: Attend the 10:30 am Sunday service, which has staffed childcare for infants and toddlers. Send children to Sunday school from September through July, or look into the community and mission programs.

schedule.text: Sunday service at 10:30 am in the upstairs sanctuary. Sunday school classes run September through July, and children take part in the first part of worship with their parents.

access.notes: A ramp on the west side of the building leads to the foyer, and an elevator there goes up to the sanctuary. The accessible restroom is on the first floor next to the nursery. Ask a greeter at the main entrance for help.

first_step.how: Attend the 10:30 am Sunday service in the upstairs sanctuary. To ask about Sunday school for children, email Pastor Rebecca at rebecca@oldpine.org.
first_step.basis: The site says visitors are welcome and expected, explains childcare and Sunday school, and gives the worship time, but names no separate newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: The 10:30 am service is held in the upstairs sanctuary, which has a historic pipe organ. A choir sings most Sundays from September to mid-June, an in-house bluegrass band plays at services through the year, and coffee hour follows worship. The site does not say how long the service lasts, what to wear, or whether there is a cost.
first_visit_tips: Park in the free lot on the east side of 5th Street between Lombard and Pine, or ask a greeter for a placard for on-street parking on Lombard between 3rd and 5th.
The loading zone in front of the main entrance at 412 Pine Street can be used to drop off people with mobility needs.
Staffed nursery care is available for infants and toddlers during worship.
Coffee hour follows worship on Sundays, if you want to stay and meet people.

records.notes: The parking and accessibility PDF on the site has no printed date. The children's page and the worship page give different age ranges for Sunday school, so the schedule text avoids an age range. Youth groups meet as needed and no days are listed. The 2026-10 evidence from tier 1 could not be reconfirmed on this visit (the site shows only a 2020 footer year), so the tier 1 value is kept.

records.name: Old St. Joseph's Parish
records.summary: A historic Catholic parish at 4th and Walnut Streets with three Sunday Masses and a weekday lunchtime Mass on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, or ask the priest presiding at daily Mass about confession. The Archdiocese listing names no parish groups.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 7:30, 9:30 and 11:30 am. Weekday Mass on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday at 12:05 pm, and at 12:05 pm on holy days.

access.notes: The Archdiocese listing says the church restroom is wheelchair accessible, one meeting room has accessible entrances and facilities, and the church has an assistive listening system. It does not describe step-free access to the main church.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass (7:30, 9:30 or 11:30 am) or the weekday Mass at 12:05 pm on Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday, or call the rectory at 215-923-1733.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone, the Archdiocese listing gives a rectory phone, and no newcomer program is listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone. Sunday Masses are at 7:30, 9:30 and 11:30 am, and weekday Mass is at 12:05 pm on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. The Archdiocese listing says you ask the priest presiding at daily Mass to hear your confession, and it does not say how long Mass runs or what to wear.
first_visit_tips: The church is at 4th and Walnut Streets; the Archdiocese lists the rectory at 321 Willings Alley.
The church has an assistive listening system, as the Archdiocese listing describes.
Call the rectory at 215-923-1733 to confirm holy day times before you come.

records.notes: The parish's own website returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch, so nothing from it is recorded; the facts come from the Archdiocese listing at archphila.org. A search summary mentioned a Saturday 5:30 pm vigil, a Sunday 6:30 pm Mass, and a different confession schedule, and an older history mentioned outreach programs; none of these were confirmed on a page I could read, so they are left out. The rectory email is hidden on the Archdiocese listing and is not recorded.

records.name: Old St. Mary's Parish
records.summary: A historic Catholic parish in Old City with a Sunday Mass at 10 am and weekday morning Mass.
records.what_you_do: Join the Sunday 10 am Mass or a weekday morning Mass. The Archdiocese page lists no other public programs.

schedule.text: Saturday vigil Mass at 4:30 pm, Sunday Mass at 10 am, and weekday Mass Monday to Friday at 7:30 am.

locations.label: Chapel of the former convent (weekday Mass)

first_step.how: Come to the Sunday 10 am Mass or the Saturday 4:30 pm vigil, or call the rectory at 215-923-7930 to ask about parish life.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone and the rectory phone is listed; no newcomer program is listed on the site or the Archdiocese page.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone. Sunday Mass is at 10 am, the Saturday vigil at 4:30 pm, and weekday Mass at 7:30 am Monday to Friday in the chapel of the former convent at 5th and Locust. Confession is heard on Saturdays at 4 pm, and neither the parish site nor the bulletin page we could read lists any groups for newcomers.
first_visit_tips: Weekday Mass is held in the chapel of the former convent at 5th and Locust, not in the main church.
For baptism information, call the rectory at 215-923-7930.
The rectory is at 252 S. 4th Street.

records.notes: The bulletin link on the parish site leads to a bulletin page dated October 11, 2026 for Old Saint Mary Church and Holy Trinity Church, sharing the same rectory. The full bulletin PDF was not readable, so any groups printed there are unknown. Mass times agree between the parish site and the Archdiocese page.

records.name: Old Tennis Court Farm
records.summary: A community garden in Germantown on Wissahickon Avenue where members grow food on their own plots and share about 8 hours a season of upkeep.
records.what_you_do: Join the waitlist for a plot (the garden is full for 2026). Members grow food on their plots, help with shared upkeep, and many donate produce to Germantown groups.

first_step.how: Join the waitlist through the Google form on the membership page, since the garden is full for 2026, or email oldtenniscourtfarm@yahoo.com with questions.
first_step.basis: Membership is closed for the 2026 season; the only listed way in is a waitlist form, and the page gives no wait time or open dates.
first_step.what_to_expect: Members get a plot of about 12 by 12 feet (some are half that size) and volunteer about 8 hours a season on shared work such as weeding, mowing, compost, trash pickup, snow removal, and website work. The page welcomes gardeners of every experience level and children of all ages. It does not state a membership fee, workday dates, or open days.
first_visit_tips: The page lists no open days, so email before you plan a visit.
Join the waitlist even though the garden is full for 2026, since that is the only listed way in.
If you join, plan on about 8 hours of shared work each season.

records.notes: The membership page on the garden's own site (oldtenniscourtfarm.org) says the garden is full for the 2026 season and that the waitlist uses the same Google form as membership. An earlier homepage summary mentioned a .com address that did not resolve, so it is not used. The community outreach page returned 404. The ngtrust profile gives 2011 as the founding year and 2018 as the preservation year.
